cis_text.title: Conduct Threat Modeling

ai_guidance.llm: Perform threat modeling specifically for AI systems to identify unique attack vectors like adversarial examples or inversion attacks. Proactively identifies design flaws and security gaps in AI systems before they can be exploited in production, improving overall system resilience.
ai_guidance.agent: Perform threat modeling for agent systems, considering unique threats like prompt injection, goal misalignment, and tool abuse. This proactively identifies security design flaws and attack vectors specific to agents, enabling the implementation of effective mitigations before deployment.
ai_guidance.mcp: Repeat threat modeling when MCP capability sets, authorization flows, server configurations, or deployment patterns change. New tool registrations, third-party server additions, protocol version updates, and gateway policy changes all expand or shift the attack surface in ways that invalidate prior assessments. Treat capability additions and authorization flow changes as mandatory threat model update triggers, not just development milestones.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
